blueprint.scientific_analysis: Frisson in blues is neurologically driven by dopaminergic anticipation-reward cycles triggered by unexpected harmonic violations and sudden dynamic contrasts that activate the anterior cerebellum and nucleus accumbens. The golden ratio emotional peak (~61.8% track duration) exploits temporal expectancy mechanisms, maximizing autonomic arousal through skin conductance response and piloerection pathways.
blueprint.structure: The track opens with sparse, tension-building fingerpicked blues guitar in E, utilizing bent notes and unresolved dominant seventh chords that create mounting melodic anxiety over 32 bars. At the golden ratio moment (approximately 2:30 of a 4:00 track), a sudden explosive shift from dead silence to full band entry occurs simultaneously with an unexpected modulation to the flattened sixth chord (C major from E), delivering maximum harmonic surprise. The track resolves through a classic turnaround progression with descending bass line, releasing accumulated tension and completing the neurological reward cycle.
